title: fix: record serving models consistently in Tinybird
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Fixes mixed `model_used` values by recording the canonical public model that served each attempt, including failed attempts and hidden provider fallbacks. Keeps caller input/aliases in `model_requested`, the primary public model in `resolved_model_requested`, and the serving supplier in `model_provider_used`. Addresses #14543.
- Keeps public IDs stable across provider changes. Adds registry checks against duplicate public IDs across modalities and reuse of retired bundled IDs, including as aliases.
- Uses existing Tinybird columns and updates their explanatory comments. Historical rows remain unchanged. No new datasource columns, endpoints, pricing changes, or routing changes; cost-coverage reporting is outside this PR.
- Validation: full GitHub CI passed, plus 698 focused local tests, Gen/Enter typechecks, and Biome after merging current main. Attribution tests cover successful and failed requests, provider routes, cross-model fallbacks, embeddings, and realtime.

gist.headline: The ledger knows who buzzed
gist.blurb: Tinybird now records the canonical public model that actually served every generation attempt, even when a hidden fallback takes the pollen. Cleaner attribution, fewer mysterious model names.
gist.summary: Generation tracking now records the canonical public serving model in `model_used` for successful and failed attempts, while preserving caller input in `model_requested`, the primary public model in `resolved_model_requested`, and the supplier in `model_provider_used`.
gist.impact: Model-health and earnings reporting can consistently attribute requests across provider fallbacks, embeddings, realtime requests, and retired-model safeguards without changing public IDs, routing, pricing, or existing historical rows.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy observability garden: Polli acts as a careful librarian, labeling jars of nectar with the public model that actually produced them while a CRT robot traces a hidden fallback vine back to its source. Small code-plants and a tidy ledger represent stable model IDs and reliable reporting.
